title: Use word boundaries in validate_plan banned-token check
problem: runner/validate_plan.py::_check_banned_tokens uses naive substring matching against the planner's code_spec and description text. Substrings like 'from requests' falsely match legitimate non-banned imports such as 'from requests_mock import ...', rejecting valid plans and eroding trust in the validator.
description:
Convert _check_banned_tokens from substring matching to word-boundary regex matching.

Each entry in _BANNED_TOKENS becomes a precompiled regex with appropriate word boundaries:
- 'pytest' -> r'\bpytest\b'
- 'shell=true' -> r'\bshell\s*=\s*True\b' (case-insensitive)
- 'import requests' -> r'\bimport\s+requests\b'
- 'from requests' -> r'\bfrom\s+requests\b'

Keep the {token: reason} mapping shape so the error messages still surface the human-readable reason on retry. Compile the regexes once at module level.

Add tests covering: 'pytest' alone still rejected; 'pytest_mock' alone NOT rejected (boundary works); 'from requests_mock import' NOT rejected; 'from requests import get' still rejected; 'shell=True' (real spelling) still rejected; case variants of shell=True still rejected.
context: Filed as scribe TODO #239 during the #212 follow-up review. Pure refinement of an existing check; no new validation surface, no behavior change for legitimate use.
